cells.tense: The pull you are following right now is a real one and it has already carried you somewhere.
cells.ask: Put one thing you've actually made in front of one person this week. Show it, don't explain it.
cells.core:
There's a way this runs when it's going well: you move toward something because you want it, and you keep wanting it past a boring Tuesday. You can tell the pull that's yours from the bright thing beside it, and people near you feel the direction without you announcing it. Underneath, something you stayed with has come along on its own — what shows now isn't performance, it's the result standing quietly after the work that made it.
The next move is small and public. Set one thing you made where somebody can see it, and don't walk them through it. What comes back feeds it, and whether or not anyone says the right thing, it stays yours.

cells.tense: You will be talking about a version of this that does not exist yet, and treating it as if it does.
cells.ask: Write down one thing that is actually here today. Not where it's going. Just what's already in hand.
cells.core:
There's a bright version of this you keep talking toward, and you talk about it so often it feels already true. It isn't yet. The light you keep casting forward is coming out of the room you're standing in, and the room has gotten dimmer while you've been describing the one ahead.
The pull is real. The ending you're pasting onto it isn't — some of what's actually here is unfinished, unglamorous, not yet worth describing. Look at that part once. What you write down will be small. It will also be the first thing in a while you've actually seen.

cells.tense: You used to feel that pull, and somewhere along the way it stopped reaching you, or you stopped reaching for it.
cells.ask: Water one plant, or sit with one person having a hard week. Same small gesture several days, no announcement.
cells.core:
When this is running well, the lean toward light is steady and unhurried — you move toward what you care about, and the moving itself keeps something warm in you. What's here instead is flatness. Things you once cared about sit there without pulling, and asking yourself to hope again only makes the quiet louder. That's where this one leaves you standing.
What tends to come back is smaller and more physical: tending something that can't thank you properly. A plant, a person having a bad week, a page you fill in badly. It comes back through the hand, not the mind. Give it a few days of that before deciding anything about it.

cells.tense: You are already the one steering this, and you have been calling it somebody else's doing or nobody's.
cells.ask: Name one decision you've been treating as outside you. Say to one person, plainly: that pick was mine.
cells.core:
This runs well when the person knows they're the one choosing — the pull gets felt, picked up, followed on purpose, and owned out loud. What's happening instead is that the steps keep getting taken and the credit keeps landing elsewhere. Luck, timing, somebody else wanted it, it just worked out. The movement is real and the hand is yours; the account just leaves you out of it.
Take one decision back. Not the whole life — one. Say out loud that you chose it, to somebody who can hear it in your ordinary voice. Then check what's still pulling. Some of that forward lean may have been waiting for you to stand under it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person has already produced something that has come to be — the record gives the card's exact many times, not the person's history. People bad at receiving accounts of themselves will likely say the radiance reading is flattery and the exhaustion reading is a diagnosis, and either refusal should still leave them a task. The ask survives a wrong read because its object is external and small — a sentence, a written thing, a named account, a hand held through one blankness — and each one teaches something about this capacity even if the read is off. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any graceful conflation of flaw and gift, so that has been cut from every cell.
